items.title: langchain-ai / langgraph
items.summary: LangGraph is a low-level orchestration framework for building, managing, and deploying long-running, stateful agents. It provides infrastructure for durable execution, human-in-the-loop oversight, and comprehensive memory, and can be used standalone or integrated with LangChain products.
items.why_it_matters: It enables the construction of agents that persist through failures and resume from exact states, while offering tools to inspect and modify agent state during execution.
items.next_step_detail: pip install langgraph && explore the quick‑start example in the repo.

items.title: headroomlabs-ai / headroom
items.summary: Headroom compresses tool outputs, logs, RAG chunks, files, and conversation history locally before they reach the LLM, reducing input tokens by 21–57% on agent scenarios and over 90% on repeated JSON arrays and log lines. It preserves answers by caching originals locally for on-demand retrieval via a CCR mechanism.
items.why_it_matters: It reduces input token usage for AI agents and applications by compressing data locally without sending content to external services.
items.next_step_detail: pip install headroom && integrate its proxy in your agent's request pipeline.

items.title: asgeirtj / system_prompts_leaks
items.summary: A repository continuously scrapes and publishes the hidden system prompts of over 30 commercial LLM chatbots, including ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, with daily updates. It has been cited by The Washington Post and Simon Willison as a definitive source for these leaked instructions.
items.why_it_matters: The repository provides the full text of hidden system prompts for every version of popular chatbots since May 2025, allowing users to see the specific rules governing model behavior.
items.next_step_detail: Audit any internal prompts or prompt‑engineering pipelines and remove reliance on leaked content.

items.title: Can't Beat Free: Gemma 4 31B on AMD Token Lab, with a Local Chat Page and an ADK Agent
items.summary: A guide demonstrates running the 31-billion-parameter Gemma 4 model on AMD GPUs via the free AMD Token Lab API, which requires no credit card or request. The setup includes a local chat UI and a small ADK agent that utilize the API's tool calling and JSON output capabilities.
items.why_it_matters: The API provides a free, OpenAI-compatible endpoint with a 262,144-token context and support for tool calling, allowing developers to build and test agents on AMD hardware without financial barriers.
items.next_step_detail: Follow the dev.to guide to register on AMD Token Lab, launch the local chat page, and invoke the ADK agent.

items.title: uv for AWS Lambda: Packaging Python Dependencies
items.summary: A guide demonstrates building arm64 Linux wheels from a uv.lock file for AWS Lambda layers without Docker, ensuring dependencies match the cloud architecture. It uses uv to install platform-specific packages on local machines like Mac or Windows, avoiding the need for Docker or matching CI runners.
items.why_it_matters: It prevents runtime ImportErrors caused by binary or Python version mismatches by ensuring the deployed layer contains the exact Linux wheels required for the Lambda environment.
items.next_step_detail: Follow the article steps to run `uv export --format requirements.txt` then `uv pip install -r requirements.txt -t ./layer` for Lambda.

items.title: Anthropic Upgrades Claude Code Projects to Run Parallel AI Workers Hands-Free
items.summary: Anthropic added proactive coordinator messages, read‑only thread sharing, reminders, branching commands and better artifact navigation to Claude Code Projects. The coordinator orchestrates multiple independent Claude cloud sessions, each with its own repo copy and Git branch, reducing manual monitoring of parallel workers.
items.why_it_matters: Enables building multi‑agent coding workflows with less orchestration overhead, directly applicable to autonomous agent pipelines.
items.next_step_detail: Sign up for Claude Code Projects and run a simple two‑thread example following the documentation.

items.title: Unsloth Qwen3.8-27B Quantizations – Dynamic v3.1 Update
items.summary: The Qwen3.8-27B 27‑billion‑parameter model now runs locally on 17 GB RAM/VRAM using Unsloth GGUFs with Dynamic V3.1 quantization, boosting accuracy 5‑10% while keeping size comparable. It supports vision, reasoning, a 256K context window, and agentic coding tasks.
items.why_it_matters: Provides a high‑performing, locally runnable LLM for agentic coding and RAG workloads without cloud costs.
items.next_step_detail: Install Unsloth, download the Qwen3.8‑27B GGUF and run the provided inference script on your workstation.

items.title: alibaba / open-code-review

items.next_step_detail: Compare its feature set and API to your current review automation (e.g., ReviewGPT) and run a pilot on a small repo.
